A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoT-generalization study despite retitling and reorganization. Their main text, equations, six figures, four tables, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original controlled training experiments, circuit analyses, noise studies, and GSM8K fine-tuning results, including supplementary experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds qualitative weight-reuse and three-hop circuit findings in Section 4 and Appendix D.4.

M1.justification: Section 4 adds an inference adaptation that reuses trained weights at twice the depth and predicts the final entity from a masked-position hidden state. The main CoT/non-CoT training procedures remain unchanged; the newly written loss definitions do not establish a training-method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic one-, two-, and three-hop facts, the same noisy scenarios, MetaMathQA/GSM8K, and Wikidata-based two-hop queries. The added mechanistic probes reuse existing reasoning tasks. Real-world experiments move to Appendix E without changing coverage.

E2.justification: The CoT/non-CoT comparisons and pretrained versus answer-only fine-tuning baselines are retained. V2 Table 1 and v3 Table 4 contain the same Llama3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-3B comparisons; v3 corrects the earlier prose's Llama3-8B label to match the existing table.

E3.justification: The added Section 4 test introduces doubled depth with weight reuse, input e1,r1,r2,[mask], and inspection of the final-layer masked-position representation. Existing experiments retain their documented splits, training budgets, model configurations, and noise settings.

E4.justification: V3 adds a weight-reuse probe asking whether multi-step reasoning can occur within one computational process. Appendix D.4 also adds circuit analysis of the already studied three-hop-trained model. Existing ratio, depth, noise, length-generalization, and gradient analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging the first-hop-noise table over three random seeds (v2 Table 4; v3 Table 3), and retain the same plotted shaded bands. V3 introduces no additional repeated-run information or statistical uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: V3 newly reports correct final-entity prediction in the masked-input weight-reuse test and a three-stage circuit activating successive pairs e1,r1; r2,e2; and r3,e3. Existing numerical results remain unchanged, including GSM8K CoT scores of 74.01% and 78.81% in v2 Table 1 and v3 Table 4.

T1.justification: V3 Definition 1 explicitly defines CoT as a complete reasoning-state sequence and gives its conditional factorization; Definition 3 formalizes training and test losses. The three principal theorems, corollaries, assumptions, and appendix proofs are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The central convergence, ID/OOD generalization, robustness, and staged-circuit claims remain. V3 emphasizes compositional reuse of learned skills and adds a conclusion-level claim that clear decomposition of reasoning steps is more critical to CoT-data quality than answer correctness alone.

C2.justification: Section 4 adds an optimization interpretation contrasting decomposed skill learning with direct answer matching, qualified by acceptable error accumulation. Section 6 newly acknowledges that simpler learned skills are difficult to identify in real-world tasks; v2's limitations addressed latent reasoning and reinforcement fine-tuning.

D1.justification: Definition 3 explicitly distinguishes generated-intermediate autoregression from teacher forcing, expanding v2's input/output description. Section 4 documents the added masked-input weight-reuse setup. Existing optimizer settings, LoRA configurations, hardware information, and code-access statement remain.

R1.justification: V3 adds references on next-token prediction and further theoretical/CoT work, plus Yuan et al.'s skill-composition account in the limitations. These extend the context without substantially replacing the existing positioning relative to CoT prompting, latent reasoning, distillation, and loop transformers.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around compositional generalization. Theory moves before the experimental setup, a discussion section is introduced, real-world validation moves into Appendix E, and the related-work and proof appendices exchange order.

P2.justification: The six figures retain their graphics, with limited circuit-caption revisions. The GSM8K table moves from the main text to Appendix E, noise tables are regrouped, and conference headers and section typography change the layout. No new figure or table is introduced.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the compositional account more explicit, adds limited mechanistic support through the weight-reuse and three-hop circuit checks, and acknowledges a concrete real-world applicability limitation absent from v2. These modestly improve explanation and support. The new checks remain qualitative without accuracy or sample-size reporting, while the quantitative evidence and central proofs are unchanged.
